title: Preface
summary: This document outlines the comprehensive syllabus for the 'Advanced Route of Learning AI' course offered by Krish Naik Academy for the 2025-2026 cohort. The curriculum spans 21 modules, covering foundational topics like Neural Networks and Transformers, progressing to advanced concepts such as Scaling Laws, Mixture of Experts (MoE), and extensive LLM fine-tuning techniques (including PEFT, SFT, and post-training stacks). It also delves into specialized areas like Reasoning Models, SLMs, Hybrid Architectures (SSMs, Mamba, RWKV), Vision and Visual Language Models, Diffusion Transformers, Embeddings, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) with multi-modal and security aspects, Context Engineering, DSPy for programmatic LLM optimization, Agents, and Reinforcement Learning (RL). The syllabus includes hardware considerations, tokenization, KV cache, attention variants, positional encodings, and knowledge distillation.

## MODULE 4

title: Tokenization Deep Dive
summary: This text provides a deep dive into tokenization strategies, covering classical methods like BPE and WordPiece, as well as advanced token-free approaches such as Byte Latent Transformers. It details the taxonomy of tokenization (word, subword, character, byte levels) and specific algorithms (Byte pair coding, Word piece, Sentence piece). The text then explores the limitations of traditional tokenizers and introduces Byte Latent Transformers, explaining their byte-level concept, architecture (including the entropy-based patching mechanism and three-component design: Local Encoder, Latent Global Transformer, Local Decoder), and a new scaling dimension. Finally, it compares tokenization with BLT. The content is presented as part of Krish Naik Academy's Advanced Route of Learning AI for the 2025-2026 Cohort, specifically within Module 5.

title: Knowledge Distillation
summary: This text provides a comprehensive overview of Knowledge Distillation, covering fundamental concepts like the student-teacher paradigm, the nature of knowledge, and different distillation techniques. It details response-based distillation using soft labels, including temperature scaling and KL divergence loss, as well as feature-based distillation with hint layers and attention transfer, exemplified by DistilBERT and TinyBERT. The text also explores relation-based distillation, black-box LLM distillation (including Orca, DeepSeek-R1, MiniLLM, and NVIDIA Minitron), white-box distillation, and sequence-level KD. A practical guide to building a distillation pipeline is presented, along with the concept of cross-architecture and cross-task distillation. The content is associated with Krish Naik Academy.

title: Hybrid Architectures — SSMs, Mamba, RWKV & Beyond Transformers
prefix_summary: This document explores hybrid AI architectures that go beyond traditional Transformers, focusing on State Space Models (SSMs), Mamba, and RWKV. It details the limitations of Transformers due to complexity, introduces the mathematical foundations of SSMs, and explains why early SSMs struggled with language tasks. Mamba is presented as a selective SSM with input-dependent parameters and a hardware-aware parallel scan, offering $O(n)$ performance and future iterations like Mamba-2 and Mamba-3. RWKV is described as an RNN-Transformer hybrid utilizing a dual-mode approach for training and inference, with its version history and key components outlined. The text then compares Mamba and RWKV, presenting performance benchmarks. It delves into hybrid architectures in general, highlighting their design philosophy and the continued relevance of pure SSMs. Specific hybrid models like Jamba (Transformer + Mamba + MoE) and Kimi (Linear Attention, KDA, 3:1 Hybrid Ratio) are discussed, along with NVIDIA's Nemotron-H and Nemotron 3 (Hybrid MoE). Finally, it touches upon routing trade-offs and other hybrid models like Zamba and Bamba.
text:
